title: Ephemeral runbook cache and idempotent rollforward handler for safe post-incident triage
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds ephemeral runbook caching to speed on-call lookups and an idempotent rollforward handler to safely apply automated remediations during triage. Backwards-compatible; no config changes required for existing playbooks.
description: Context and motivation: On high-noise incidents the incident-bot runbook lookups and remediation orchestration were adding 150-300ms per request and occasionally executing non-idempotent handlers twice when a race in the triage state machine retried a step. This PR introduces a bounded ephemeral runbook cache (in-memory with TTL and stale-while-revalidate) to reduce lookup latency, and a 'rollforward' handler wrapper that enforces idempotency and safe retries for automated remediation actions. Goals: 1) reduce median oncall lookup latency under load, 2) prevent double-applies of non-idempotent remediation steps, 3) preserve existing runbook semantics and allow opt-out via annotation. Changes summary: - runbook cache: lightweight LRU with 1s default TTL, 5s stale-while-revalidate, metrics and per-team tunables - rollforward handler: decorator that records ephemeral execution tokens in the triage transaction store and rejects duplicates or replays; supports compensating actions and safe-noop return codes - migrations: small schema bump to triage transactions to add an executions map (backfilled lazily) - safety: feature flag off by default for first week, auto-fallback to existing behavior on store errors - telemetry: tracing spans, histogram of cache hit/miss, counter for suppressed duplicate executions Why this approach: persistent caching at the platform level would add operational complexity and cross-tenant leak risk. An ephemeral per-instance cache with clear TTLs gives the latency wins while remaining safe for multi-tenant deployments. The rollforward decorator centralizes idempotency logic so individual runbook steps do not need bespoke guards. Backwards compatibility: runbooks without the new annotation keep current semantics. Opt-in: annotate runbook step with "idempotent: true" to enable the stronger protections. Rollout plan: feature-flag gated, dogfood enabled for SRE, staged rollout to 20% of instances on 2025-11-07, monitor cache hit ratio and suppressed-exec counts, ramp to 100% after 72h if no anomalies. Related work: follow-up will add persistent per-team cache and richer compensator registry (ENG-4899). || Commits summary: - 64a2b3d: initial runbook cache implementation and unit tests - 7f1c8b2: add stale-while-revalidate + metrics and config knobs - b2d98f1: rollforward handler, decorator API, and integration tests - c3e9f34: triage transaction schema bump and migration shim - d11a7e0: safety feature flag + toggles in ops console - e4f5a90: docs and runbook examples; update changelog || Files changed (high level): ["pkg/runbook/cache.go", "pkg/runbook/handler_rollforward.go", "pkg/triage/transaction_store.go", "migrations/20251103_add_exec_map.sql", "internal/flags/feature_flags.go", "docs/runbooks/idempotency.md", "pkg/runbook/cache_test.go"] || Small illustrative snippet (cache constructor): 'func NewEphemeralCache(maxEntries int, ttl time.Duration, stale time.Duration) *Cache { // LRU + TTL + stale-while-revalidate }' || Tests and CI: unit tests added for cache eviction, stale revalidate, rollforward duplicate suppression, and basic integration between triage store and handler. Local benchmarks show median lookup latency drop from 260ms to 60ms for repeated lookups under synthetic load.
